entries.gave: Read the Cut (no inputs, no decisions, no More kept; docs/product-vision.md does not exist yet), the design tree, README.md (a playground note), pyproject.toml and invoicer/ (lines.py, tax.py, totals.py, render.py: a Python library that parses semicolon-separated invoice lines, computes subtotal and tax at a rate, and renders the invoice as text; no command yet). The deliverable s people are invoicer s developers, who use the vision to know whom invoicer serves: the accounting team, who print each client s invoice at its tax rate from their spreadsheet lines, and the developers who call the library from their own code.
Read product-vision/best-practice.md (N1 to N6) with its template.md, and refactor-doc/best-practice.md (N1 to N8), to their end, before any change.
The job, from the goal and invoicer/ (the README names none): invoicer turns the lines of an invoice into the invoice, with its subtotal, tax at a rate, and total.

Roles by the part of the job they come for: one who prints a client s invoice from the lines kept in a spreadsheet (the accounting team, from the goal); one who builds invoicer s lines, totals, and invoice text into their own program (the library s callers, from the public names of invoicer/__init__.py).
The accounting team s job may need someone to install the command where they run it; neither the goal nor the repository says who, so it goes to the user.
The goal settles the accounting team s job; the library caller s job and who installs the command are unclear, so both go to the user with my guesses as recommendations.
The concept s one way and its ideas come from whoever conceived invoicer, and no input gives them, so the question goes to the user before the concept is written.
